Yes — GRAMR is a suitable platform for a six‑string 25.5" HH metal guitar and can address high‑fret access better than many standard designs. messages.content: I play metal on a six-string 25.5-inch HH guitar, not bass. High-fret access on my current guitar is awkward. Is GRAMR suitable? Recommend with reasons and price the standard build.

Yes — GRAMR is a suitable platform for a six‑string 25.5" HH metal guitar and can address high‑fret access better than many standard designs. It’s a Superstrat-style 25.5" with 24 frets, a slim 5-piece neck option and the GRAMR reference profile geared to guitar feel, so you get familiar scale/tension, compact upper‑neck reach and access designed into the shape.

Tradeoffs and ways to improve high-fret access
- Neck profile: the standard "GRAMR reference profile" is a good all-round shape. If you want noticeably easier high‑fret playing, ask about a slimmer asymmetrical or custom profile — GRAMR custom profiles are on request (we can draft questions for the maker).
- Heel and contours: GRAMR’s neck joint and 2‑piece body already favour upper‑fret access versus thicker neck‑through designs; you can ask RavenForge for more aggressive heel carving in Special Instructions.
- Fret size/radius: your current extra‑jumbo frets and 16" radius suit fast metal technique. If you prefer lower action for shredding, consider a low factory setup (for basses it's +€50, but GRAMR uses standard guitar setup included; confirm preferred setup in notes).

Price for the standard GRAMR build (your current configuration)
- Orientation — right-handed: €0

- Factory Setup — standard guitar setup: €0
- Scale — 25.5-inch single scale: €0

- Neck Profile — GRAMR reference profile: €0
- Fretboard — rosewood: €0
- Radius — 16-inch radius: €0

- Gigbag — Standard gigbag: €0

Total (estimate from configurator): €2000 (base price). This is an estimate from the configurator; RavenForge will confirm the final price.

Next step
- If you want I can suggest specific changes to improve upper-fret access (slimmer profile, more aggressive heel carve, or low setup) and price that recommendation.  
- When you’re ready to request a quote, please open the configurator, apply any changes and click "Save specification PDF" and send that with your enquiry.

Quick question: do you prefer a very thin, fast neck feel for shredding, or more palm‑support and substance under the thumb? This will determine the profile suggestion.
Explain my CURRENT model, fretboard, pickups and EQ, including roles and constraints.

- Model — GRAMR: a Superstrat 6‑string, 25.5" single scale with 24 frets (page: GRAMR). The design favors upper‑fret access (slim heel, 2‑piece body) and a modern neck option (5‑piece laminated guitar neck) with the GRAMR reference profile. Bridge is Gotoh 510T‑FE1, standard hardware layout and a 43.0 mm nut width.

- Fretboard — rosewood (page: Fretboard / rosewood): rosewood is warm and slightly damped compared with maple; it feels a little softer under the fingers and often balances bright pickup tones. Your configuration uses a 16‑inch radius (page: Radius) with 24 frets and no zero fret (page: Fret Type). Fret material is 18% nickel‑silver and fret size is extra jumbo (page: Fret Material / Fret Size): extra‑jumbo frets make fast bends and vibrato easier and reduce fret‑noise when fretting hard, but they raise the effective fingerboard profile slightly and can change string bending feel vs smaller frets.

- Pickups — Lundgren M6 Neck + Bridge (page: Pickups / Lundgren M6 Neck + Bridge): this is a matched HH passive humbucker set voiced for guitar; Lundgren M6s are open‑coil, focused and high‑output options well suited to metal. Constraint: pickup model and mounting follow the GRAMR HH routes; the configurator notes “retain the existing HH routes — confirm housings, mounting ears, depth and wiring” so final fit and any small routing or mounting changes must be confirmed with RavenForge.

- Onboard EQ — Zuta Core — planned (page: Onboard EQ / Zuta Core — planned): listed as “planned” for GRAMR; it’s included in the current selection but the catalog warns “guitar electronics package; final wiring to be confirmed.” That means the basic passive control layout (page: Controls & Wiring / 1 Volume / 1 Tone / 5‑way blade) is used now, but the final Zuta Core wiring, features and any active functions or battery requirements will need RavenForge confirmation before build.

If you want, I can suggest changes (slimmer profile, compound radius, or different pickups/EQ) to further improve high‑fret playability or tone. Which matter most: easier upper‑neck reach or a very low action for shredding?
Compare standard GRAMR with GRAMR using an ebony fretboard. Keep other options standard. Explain both totals and the difference; price the latter last. I have not accepted it; do not apply.

The configurator returned the same total (€2000) but did not apply the change: ebony is not available for GRAMR in the standard options. The price result therefore remains the GRAMR standard total (€2000) and there is no priced “ebony” line.

What this means and alternatives
- You can keep the included rosewood board (no price change) and the quoted €2000 stands as the estimate.
- If you want an ebony board, ask RavenForge for an "other" fretboard (exotic) via the Fretboard category — those requests are handled on request and the total will be incomplete until RavenForge confirms material availability and price.
- Pickups and Zuta Core: Lundgren M6 and the planned Zuta Core are included in the standard total; final wiring/fit for Zuta Core will be confirmed by RavenForge (not a priced extra).

You have not accepted the ebony change; it was not applied. If you want, I can:
- Price a requested exotic fretboard (on request) by composing questions for the maker, or
- Suggest and price a different available fretboard option (if any) — tell me which.
